note: Approximate, typical conditions, not forecasts. Summit (~8,600 m, ~325–350 hPa): monthly means read from published ERA5 climatology charts (1979–2021); range = ±1 standard deviation of daily wind. Base camp (~5,000 m): NASA POWER/MERRA-2 24-hour mean, 2001–2020.

months.name: January
months.summary: Jet stream overhead: summit winds about 95 km/h, air about −45 °C. The first winter summit (16 Jan 2021) needed a rare calm ridge.

months.name: February
months.summary: Deep winter continues: summit air about −45 °C with jet-stream winds near 95 km/h. Hardly any day is calm enough to climb.

months.name: March
months.summary: Still winter aloft: summit winds about 85 km/h, air near −42 °C. The jet stream only starts weakening late in the month.

months.name: April
months.summary: The jet stream starts drifting north and winds drop to about 65 km/h, but summit air is still near −37 °C.

months.name: May
months.summary: Winds ease to near-summer levels (about 55 km/h) yet summit air stays around −33 °C. Expeditions have not arrived yet.

months.name: June
months.summary: Expeditions arrive and fix ropes. Summit warms to about −27 °C with winds near 55 km/h; summit bids before July are rare.

months.name: July
months.summary: Best month: warmest summit air (about −21 °C), winds near 55 km/h, weak monsoon influence. Over 90% of summits happen in July, mostly late.

months.name: August
months.summary: Early August is still mild (about −21 °C, winds near 55 km/h). A few summits seep into mid-August, then teams head home.

months.name: September
months.summary: Summit cools to about −27 °C, winds near 60 km/h. Most expeditions have left; autumn ascents are rare (one was September 1978).

months.name: October
months.summary: Summit near −35 °C with winds around 60 km/h and rising. A couple of October summits happened decades ago, none recently.

months.name: November
months.summary: The jet stream returns: summit winds about 80 km/h, air near −40 °C. Base camp averages around −18 °C.

months.name: December
months.summary: Full winter: summit winds about 95 km/h and air near −43 °C. Winter expeditions arrive to face jet-stream storms.

sources.title: Matthews et al. (2021), 'Weather on K2 during historic first winter ascent', Weather (RMetS), doi:10.1002/wea.4094 — accepted manuscript, Loughborough University repository
sources.used_for: Month-by-month summit temperature and wind speed (and ±1 SD wind range), digitised from Fig. 2 ERA5 day-of-year climatology (1979–2021) interpolated to K2's summit; winter 2020/21 extremes; 16 Jan 2021 ridge.

sources.title: Szymczak et al. (2021), 'Comparison of Environmental Conditions on Summits of Mount Everest and K2 in Climbing and Midwinter Seasons', IJERPH 18:3040
sources.used_for: Cross-check of ERA5 summit means: July −21 ± 1 °C / 15 ± 3 m/s; January and February −45 °C / 27 ± 4 m/s; summit pressure 325–347 hPa; jet-stream explanation (weakens and shifts north in summer).

sources.title: Szymczak et al. (2021), 'Death Zone Weather Extremes Mountaineers Have Experienced in Successful Ascents', Frontiers in Physiology
sources.used_for: K2 climbing season in July and August; summit-day conditions averaging −19 °C and 12 ± 5 m/s; 16 Jan 2021 winter summit at about −40 °C and 5 m/s.

sources.title: NASA POWER Climatology API — MERRA-2 2-m air temperature, 2001–2020, grid point 35.83°N 76.51°E (grid elevation 5,153 m)
sources.used_for: Monthly base-camp temperatures (24-hour mean T2M, rounded to 1 °C).

sources.used_for: Cross-check: measured mean daytime (06–18 h) temperature at K2 base camp of 2.1 °C, 8 July–4 August 2004.

sources.title: FAO Mountain Partnership, 'Monitoring K2 climate data in real time' (SHARE station near K2 Base Camp, July 2014)
sources.used_for: Cross-check: first readings at the 4,970 m base-camp station ranged −1 to 6.9 °C in July.

sources.title: Alan Arnette, 'K2 Summer 2022: Weekend Update July 30, 2022 – A Summer of Summits'
sources.used_for: Well over 90% of K2 summits occur in July; some seep into mid-August; a couple of October summits decades ago.

sources.title: Alan Arnette, 'K2 2026: Coverage Begins & First Summits'
sources.used_for: Most K2 summits occur at the end of July.

sources.title: Elite Exped, 'The Best Season for a Successful K2 Climb' (secondary, operator write-up)
sources.used_for: Season framing (mid-June to September, best July–August); base camp around 6 °C in summer; winter base camp −30 °C by day, −40 °C at night (suggests 24-hour reanalysis means understate winter cold at camp).

sources.title: Alan Arnette, 'Winter K2 Update: Chillin' at Base Camp' (6 Jan 2021)
sources.used_for: Context only: winter 2021 base-camp reports of temperatures down to −50 °C and hurricane-strength winds.

sources.title: NOAA GFDL research highlight on Kapnick et al. (2014), Nature Geoscience: 'Karakoram snowfall less sensitive to warming than Himalayas due to a unique seasonal cycle'
sources.used_for: Karakoram precipitation comes mostly from winter westerlies, whereas the rest of the Himalaya is monsoon-dominated (weak monsoon influence in July).
